reads.what: The World Desk numbers on the masthead ear and the WorldGlyph caption, and how each was produced.
reads.escalation_index: escalation_index = (sum of severity over registry proxies past their frozen threshold) / (sum of severity over all registry proxies). It measures conflict-linked market and energy stress over this fixed population, on a 0-1 scale. It is not a forecast and not a count of wars. Thresholds were frozen before this reading: each threshold is that series' p80 over the 5 years ending at minted_at, computed by sensors/automation/mint-escalation-registry.mjs.
reads.open_conflicts: Corroborated in THIS edition's story corpus by at least `open_min_stories` distinct stories, each carrying at least one source URL in its own prepared filing block. A story with no retrievable URL is not corroboration.
reads.watch: One of the two mechanically distinct reasons to keep an eye on a place: either it drew at least `watch_min_stories` qualifying stories this edition but fell short of the `open` bar (named, not yet stood up), or it met the `open` bar on one of the previous `watch_window_editions` editions and drew no qualifying story today. The trace records which of the two fired for every watch entry.
reads.delta: Computed against the previous DERIVED reading only. The escalation values published before this trace existed (0.72 across thirteen editions, 0.68 on 2026-09-05) were never computed and are not comparable, so the first derived edition prints "first reading" rather than a direction against a number that was never a measurement.

escalation.formula: index = sum(severity where triggering) / sum(severity over all entries)

not_measured: This index measures conflict-linked market and energy stress, not conflict. Every proxy is a price, a spread or a volatility index; a war that moves no market moves this number not at all.
Flashpoint matching is deterministic keyword matching over story prose, not entity resolution. Each counted entry lists the terms that fired and the story they fired on so a wrong match is arguable.
